# pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 7, 2026 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in `pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image build) carries no JNA. ## Implemented - **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`, `Commands` (incl. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`. - **Attributed text** (`dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`): pure-Kotlin model + range-tracking builder (Kotlin char indices → UTF-8 byte offsets) and payload encode/decode; `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal)` emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` through the emitter and both sinks. - **Built-in inline Markdown**: `Text("...")` parses the v1 subset by default (`**bold**`/`__bold__`, `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`); `markdown = false` renders literal text. `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is now a **pure-Java parser** (no native library, so it runs on every platform and under GraalVM native-image); it is a behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-markdown` crate (pre-scan + bounded cache). The Rust crate remains the parser for the Rust DSL and non-JVM hosts. Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path; rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive `Text(Signal)` parses on change. - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/ `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState` during a component render. - **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly typed `Topic` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)` declares an unscoped `Topic` with the two-argument `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal` backed by a session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local, installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes `unsubscribe` and `submit`. Resolution is lazy when a root view's field initializer runs before the context is installed. - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and annotation processor are removed. - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`, `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`. **Hardened (issue #63)**: `FrameCodec.parse` reads the attacker-controlled `opcodeCount`/`stringsLen` as unsigned `Long` values and validates them against the actual message length before allocating; string offsets are bounds-checked (`Parsed.stringAt`). A declared `opcodeCount` that overflows `Int` arithmetic now throws instead of triggering an OOM allocation. - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`, `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`, `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL. - **JNA interop**: moved to `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore`), so server runtimes do not pull JNA. - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`, `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`. Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. A replaced child is relinked to its real parent (not the tree root), so a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap cannot detach a pinned root `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` or drop its media routing. Registered `MediaController`s are projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController` removes them without touching the app tree. - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`, `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`, `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier wrappers. - **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra --- markdown head package dev.pathland.markdown; import dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString; import dev.pathland.view.core.LinkRun; import dev.pathland.view.core.StyleRun; import dev.pathland.view.core.TextAttribute; import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets; import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.Collections; import java.util.LinkedHashMap; import java.util.List; import java.util.Map; /** * Pathland's shared inline Markdown parser — a pure-Java port of the * {@code pathland-markdown} Rust crate. * *

It is pure JVM code with no native * dependency, so it runs on every platform (and under GraalVM native-image) * without a cdylib. 3: /**
4:  * Base node of the reactive graph: versioned value, producer edges, consumer
5:  * edges, dirty/first-run flags, cached error, and write guards.
6:  */
7: internal abstract class ReactiveNode(
8:     @JvmField val name: String?,
9: ) {
10:     /** A producer edge: the producer node plus its version when this node last read it. */
11:     internal class ProducerEdge(@JvmField val node: ReactiveNode) {
12:         @JvmField var lastSeenVersion: Long = node.version
13:     }
14: 
15:     @JvmField val producers: MutableList<ProducerEdge> = ArrayList()
16:     @JvmField val consumers: MutableList<ReactiveNode> = ArrayList()
17: 
18:     /** Bumped when this node's own value changes. */
19:     @JvmField var version: Long = 0
20: 
21:     /** Whether this node must (re)evaluate. */
22:     @JvmField var dirty: Boolean = true
23: 
24:     /** Whether the evaluation function has run at least once. */
25:     @JvmField var firstRun: Boolean = true
26: 
27:     /** Whether this node may write signals during its evaluation. */
28:     @JvmField var allowSignalWrites: Boolean = false
29: 
30:     /** Cached evaluation error (computed) / last run error (effect). */
31:     @JvmField var error: Throwable? = null
32: 
33:     fun describe(): String = name ?: javaClass.simpleName
34: 
35:     /** Register a dependency from the current reactive context to `this`. */
36:     fun recordDependency() {
37:         val consumer = ReactiveContext.current() ?: return
38:         val idx = consumer.indexOfProducer(this)
39:         if (idx < 0) {
40:             consumer.producers.add(ProducerEdge(this))
41:             consumers.add(consumer)
42:         } else {
43:             consumer.producers[idx].lastSeenVersion = version
44:         }
45:     }
46: 
47:     private fun indexOfProducer(producer: ReactiveNode): Int =
48:         producers.indexOfFirst { it.node === producer }
49: 
50:     /** True when at least one producer's version differs from what this node observed. */
51:     fun depsChanged(): Boolean = producers.any { it.node.version != it.lastSeenVersion }
52: 
53:     /** Drop all producer edges. */
54:     fun resetProducers() {
55:         for (edge in producers) {
56:             edge.node.consumers.remove(this)
57:         }
58:         producers.clear()
59:     }
60: 
61:     /** Re-evaluate dirty computed producers so their versions reflect value changes. */
62:     fun refreshProducers() {
63:         for (edge in producers) {
64:             val node = edge.node
65:             if (node is ComputedSignal<*>) {
66:                 node.evaluateIfDirty()
67:             }
68:         }
69:     }
70: 
71:     /** Mark every consumer dirty, schedule effects, and propagate transitively. */
72:     fun propagate() {
73:         for (consumer in consumers.toList()) {
74:             consumer.markDirtyAndPropagate()
75:         }
76:     }
77: 
78:     private fun markDirtyAndPropagate() {
79:         if (dirty) return
80:         dirty = true
81:         if (this is Effect) {
82:             schedule()
83:         }
84:         for (consumer in consumers.toList()) {
85:             consumer.markDirtyAndPropagate()
86:         }
87:     }
88: 
89:     /** Throw this node's cached evaluation error. */
90:     fun rethrowError(): Nothing {
91:         when (val t = error) {
92:             is RuntimeException -> throw t
93:             is Error -> throw t
94:             else -> throw EffectException("Reactive node '${describe()}' failed", t!!)
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:     /** Guard against signal writes inside computed/effect bodies. */
99:     fun checkWriteAllowed() {
100:         val current = ReactiveContext.current() ?: return
101:         if (current.allowSignalWrites) return
102:         throw IllegalStateException(
103:             "Signal writes are not allowed inside ${current.describe()}; " +
104:                 "pass EffectOptions.allowSignalWrites() to opt out",
105:         )
106:     }
107: }

6: /** A lazy, memoized derived signal (Angular-style `computed`). */
7: internal class ComputedSignal<T>(
8:     private val fn: Supplier<T>,
9:     private val equal: BiPredicate<T, T>,
10: ) : ReactiveNode(null), Signal<T> {
11: 
12:     private var cachedValue: T? = null
13: 
14:     override fun get(): T {
15:         if (ReactiveContext.contains(this)) {
16:             throw IllegalStateException(
17:                 "Circular signal dependency: computed '${describe()}' depends on itself",
18:             )
19:         }
20:         evaluateIfDirty()
21:         if (error != null) {
22:             rethrowError()
23:         }
24:         recordDependency()
25:         @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
26:         return cachedValue as T
27:     }
28: 
29:     fun evaluateIfDirty() {
30:         if (!dirty) return
31:         refreshProducers()
32:         dirty = false
33:         if (!firstRun && !depsChanged()) return
34:         firstRun = false
35:         ReactiveContext.push(this)
36:         resetProducers()
37:         try {
38:             val next = fn.get()
39:             if (equal.test(cachedValue as T, next)) {
40:                 error = null
41:             } else {
42:                 cachedValue = next
43:                 error = null
44:                 version++
45:                 propagate()
46:             }
47:         } catch (t: Throwable) {
48:             if (error != t) {
49:                 error = t
50:                 version++
51:                 propagate()
52:             }
53:         } finally {
54:             ReactiveContext.pop()
55:         }
56:     }

3: /** A reactive effect (Angular-style `effect`). */
4: internal class Effect(
5:     private val fn: Runnable,
6:     options: EffectOptions,
7:     name: String?,
8: ) : ReactiveNode(name), EffectRef {
9: 
10:     @JvmField var scheduled: Boolean = false
11: 
12:     init {
13:         allowSignalWrites = options.allowSignalWrites()
14:         if (!options.manualCleanup()) {
15:             schedule()
16:         }
17:     }
18: 
19:     fun schedule() {
20:         Scheduler.schedule(this)
21:     }
22: 
23:     fun runIfScheduled() {
24:         if (!dirty) return
25:         refreshProducers()
26:         dirty = false
27:         if (!firstRun && !depsChanged()) return
28:         firstRun = false
29:         ReactiveContext.push(this)
30:         val previous = producers.toList()
31:         resetProducers()
32:         try {
33:             fn.run()
34:             error = null
35:         } catch (t: Throwable) {
36:             error = t
37:             restoreProducers(previous)
38:             throw EffectException("Effect '${describe()}' threw during flush", t)
39:         } finally {
40:             ReactiveContext.pop()
41:         }
42:     }
43: 
44:     private fun restoreProducers(previous: List<ProducerEdge>) {
45:         resetProducers()
46:         for (edge in previous) {
47:             producers.add(edge)
48:             edge.node.consumers.add(this)
49:         }
50:         dirty = false
51:     }
52: 
53:     override fun destroy() {
54:         Scheduler.cancel(this)
55:         resetProducers()
56:         dirty = false
57:     }
58: }

3: import java.util.ArrayDeque
4: 
5: /** Synchronous effect scheduler (flushes to quiescence at the outermost write). */
6: internal object Scheduler {
7:     private val QUEUE = ArrayDeque<Effect>()
8:     private var flushing = false
9: 
10:     @Synchronized
11:     fun schedule(effect: Effect) {
12:         if (!effect.scheduled) {
13:             effect.scheduled = true
14:             QUEUE.add(effect)
15:         }
16:         flush()
17:     }
18: 
19:     @Synchronized
20:     fun flush() {
21:         if (flushing) return
22:         flushing = true
23:         try {
24:             while (QUEUE.isNotEmpty()) {
25:                 val effect = QUEUE.poll()
26:                 effect.scheduled = false
27:                 effect.runIfScheduled()
28:             }
29:         } finally {
30:             flushing = false
31:         }
32:     }
33: 
34:     /** Drop a destroyed effect from the queue. */
35:     @Synchronized
36:     fun cancel(effect: Effect) {
37:         QUEUE.remove(effect)
38:         effect.scheduled = false
39:     }
40: }

7: /**
8:  * Per-session persisted state. [signal] creates a signal that auto-loads its
9:  * persisted value and auto-saves on change, keyed `"name:scope"`; signals are
10:  * memoized by name.
11:  */
12: class PersistentState(
13:     private val store: StateStore,
14:     private val scope: String?,
15: ) : AutoCloseable {
16: 
17:     private val signals = HashMap<String, WritableSignal<*>>()
18:     private val persistEffects = ArrayList<EffectRef>()
19: 
20:     /** Create (or return) the signal named [name], auto-loading and auto-saving it. */
21:     @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
22:     fun <T : Any> signal(name: String, initial: T): WritableSignal<T> {
23:         val existing = signals[name] as WritableSignal<T>?
24:         if (existing != null) return existing
25: 
26:         val key = scoped(name)
27:         val signal = Signals.signal(name, store.load(key, initial.javaClass).orElse(initial))
28:         signals[name] = signal
29:         persistEffects.add(Signals.effect {
30:             try {
31:                 store.save(key, signal.get())
32:             } catch (_: RuntimeException) {
33:                 // Persistence is best-effort for a UI component.
34:             }

5: /**
6:  * The session-scoped surface available to views while they render: topic
7:  * subscriptions and a way to schedule work on the session's actor.
8:  *
9:  * A live [SessionContext] is installed by the server runtime for the duration of
10:  * every actor task (mount, dispatch, subscription drain, …), so [Topic] reads can
11:  * resolve without any explicit plumbing. Outside a session (an emitter-only unit
12:  * test, for example) [current] is `null`.
13:  */
14: interface SessionContext {
15: 
16:     /** Subscribe to [topic] for [subject], seeded with [initial]. Idempotent per `(topic, subject)`. */
17:     fun <T, S> subscribe(topic: Topic<T, S>, subject: S, initial: T): Signal<T>
18: 
19:     /** Drop the session's subscription for `(topic, subject)`. */
20:     fun <T, S> unsubscribe(topic: Topic<T, S>, subject: S)
21: 
22:     /** Run [task] on this session's actor (never on the caller's thread). */
23:     fun submit(task: Runnable)
24: 
25:     companion object {
26:         private val CURRENT = ThreadLocal<SessionContext?>()
27: 
28:         /** The session context of the current actor task, or `null`. */
29:         @JvmStatic
30:         fun current(): SessionContext? = CURRENT.get()
31: 
32:         /** Install [context] for the current thread; returns the previous one. */
33:         @JvmStatic
34:         fun push(context: SessionContext): SessionContext? {
35:             val previous = CURRENT.get()
36:             CURRENT.set(context)
37:             return previous
38:         }
39: 
40:         /** Restore the context returned by [push]. */
41:         @JvmStatic
42:         fun restore(previous: SessionContext?) {
43:             if (previous == null) CURRENT.remove() else CURRENT.set(previous)

1: package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol
2: 
3: /**
4:  * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
5:  *
6:  * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
7:  *
8:  * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
9:  * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
10:  */
11: data class Opcode(
12:     val category: Int,
13:     val command: Int,
14:     val flags: Int,
15:     val a: Int,
16:     val b: Int,
17:     val c: Int,
18: ) {
19:     fun category(): Int = category
20:     fun command(): Int = command
21:     fun flags(): Int = flags
22:     fun a(): Int = a
23:     fun b(): Int = b
24:     fun c(): Int = c
25: 
26:     /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
27:     fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
28:         val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
29:         out[0] = category.toByte()
30:         out[1] = command.toByte()
31:         out[2] = flags.toByte()
32:         out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
33:         writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
34:         writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
35:         writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
36:         return out
37:     }
38: 
39:     companion object {
40:         const val SIZE = 16
41: 
42:         /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
43:         fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
44:             require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
45:             return Opcode(
46:                 bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
47:                 bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
48:                 (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
49:                 readIntLE(bytes, 4),
50:                 readIntLE(bytes, 8),
51:                 readIntLE(bytes, 12),
52:             )
53:         }
54: 
55:         private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
56:             out[offset] = value.toByte()
57:             out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
58:             out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
59:             out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
60:         }
61: 
62:         private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
63:             (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
64:                 ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
65:                 ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
66:                 ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
67:     }
68: }

12:     fun <T> with(key: EnvironmentKey<T>, value: T): EnvironmentValues =

15:     /** The value bound to [key], walking the chain; null when absent. */
16:     @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
17:     fun <T> get(key: EnvironmentKey<T>): T? {
18:         var node: EnvironmentValues? = this
19:         while (node != null) {
20:             if (node.key === key) return node.value as T?
21:             node = node.parent
22:         }
23:         return null
24:     }
25: 
26:     /** Whether [key] is bound anywhere in the chain. */
27:     fun contains(key: EnvironmentKey<*>): Boolean {
28:         var node: EnvironmentValues? = this
29:         while (node != null) {
30:             if (node.key === key) return true
31:             node = node.parent
32:         }
33:         return false
34:     }
35: 
36:     internal fun flattened(): Map<EnvironmentKey<*>, Any?> {
37:         val out = HashMap<EnvironmentKey<*>, Any?>()
38:         var node: EnvironmentValues? = this
39:         while (node != null) {
40:             if (node.key != null && !out.containsKey(node.key)) {
41:                 out[node.key] = node.value
42:             }
43:             node = node.parent
44:         }
45:         return out
46:     }

49:         other is EnvironmentValues && flattened() == other.flattened()

8: /**
9:  * A scalar text-format attribute on a range.
10:  *
11:  * [value] is the standard 4-byte wire value (an `F32` bit pattern for float
12:  * attributes, a packed `0xAARRGGBB` for colors, `0`/`1` for booleans).
13:  */
14: data class TextAttribute(
15:     val property: Int,
16:     val valueType: Int = ValueTypes.forProperty(property),
17:     val value: Int,
18: ) {
19:     companion object {
20:         @JvmStatic fun fontSize(points: Float) =
21:             TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_SIZE, ValueTypes.F32, points.toRawBits())
22: 
23:         @JvmStatic fun fontWeight(weight: Float) =
24:             TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_WEIGHT, ValueTypes.F32, weight.toRawBits())
25: 
26:         @JvmStatic fun color(argb: Int) =
27:             TextAttribute(Properties.COLOR, ValueTypes.COLOR, argb)
28: 
29:         @JvmStatic fun italic() =
30:             TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_STYLE, ValueTypes.F32, 1.0f.toRawBits())
31: 
32:         @JvmStatic fun fontDesign(code: Int) =
33:             TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_DESIGN, ValueTypes.F32, code.toFloat().toRawBits())
34: 
35:         @JvmStatic fun underline(on: Boolean = true) =
36:             TextAttribute(Properties.UNDERLINE, ValueTypes.U8, if (on) 1 else 0)
37: 
38:         @JvmStatic fun strikethrough(on: Boolean = true) =
39:             TextAttribute(Properties.STRIKETHROUGH, ValueTypes.U8, if (on) 1 else 0)
40:     }
41: }
42: 
43: /** A range of the text with a set of scalar attributes (UTF-8 byte offsets). */
44: data class StyleRun(
45:     val start: Int,
46:     val end: Int,
47:     val attributes: List<TextAttribute>,
48: ) {
49:     fun bold() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.fontWeight(700f))
50:     fun italic() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.italic())
51:     fun monospaced() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.fontDesign(3))
52:     fun strikethrough() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.strikethrough())
53:     fun underline() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.underline())
54: 
55:     companion object {
56:         @JvmStatic fun of(start: Int, end: Int) = StyleRun(start, end, emptyList())
57:     }
58: }
59: 
60: /** A range of the text that is a hyperlink (UTF-8 byte offsets). */
61: data class LinkRun(val start: Int, val end: Int, val url: String)
62: 
63: /**
64:  * Text plus range-scoped style runs and links — the app-side model for
65:  * `PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`.
66:  *
67:  * Ranges are **UTF-8 byte offsets** (the wire convention). The [Builder] takes
68:  * Kotlin character indices and converts them at [Builder.build]; markdown
69:  * payloads decode directly into byte offsets.
70:  */
71: class AttributedString private constructor(
72:     val text: String,
73:     val runs: List<StyleRun>,
74:     val links: List<LinkRun>,
75: ) {
76:     init {
77:         val length = text.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).size
78:         for (run in runs) {
79:             require(run.start in 0..run.end && run.end <= length) {
80:                 "style run ${run.start}..${run.end} is outside the text ($length bytes)"
81:             }
82:         }
83:         for (link in links) {
84:             require(link.start in 0..link.end && link.end <= length) {
85:                 "link ${link.start}..${link.end} is outside the text ($length bytes)"
86:             }
87:         }
88:     }
89: 
90:     /** Whether this carries no style runs or links (plain text). */
91:     val isPlain: Boolean
92:         get() = runs.isEmpty() && links.isEmpty()
93: 
94:     override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean =
95:         other is AttributedString &&
96:             text == other.text &&
97:             runs == other.runs &&
98:             links == other.links
99: 
100:     override fun hashCode(): Int {
101:         var result = text.hashCode()
102:         result = 31 * result + runs.hashCode()
103:         result = 31 * result + links.hashCode()
104:         return result
105:     }
106: 
107:     override fun toString(): String =
108:         "AttributedString(text=$text, runs=$runs, links=$links)"
109: 
110:     /** Encode the `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` payload (without the arena length wrapper). */
111:     fun encode(): ByteArray {
112:         val textBytes = text.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
113:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
114:         out.writeIntLE(textBytes.size)
115:         out.write(textBytes)
116:         out.writeIntLE(runs.size)
117:         for (run in runs) {
118:             out.writeIntLE(run.start)
119:             out.writeIntLE(run.end)
120:             val supported = run.attributes.filter { isSupported(it) }
121:             out.writeIntLE(supported.size)
122:             for (attr in supported) {
123:                 out.writeShortLE(attr.property)
124:                 out.write(attr.valueType and 0xFF)
125:                 out.write(0)
126:                 out.writeIntLE(attr.value)
127:             }
128:         }
129:         out.writeIntLE(links.size)
130:         for (link in links) {
131:             val url = link.url.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
132:             out.writeIntLE(link.start)
133:             out.writeIntLE(link.end)
134:             out.writeIntLE(url.size)
135:             out.write(url)
136:         }
137:         return out.toByteArray()
138:     }
139: 
140:     companion object {
141:         private val SUPPORTED = setOf(
142:             Properties.FONT_SIZE,
143:             Properties.FONT_WEIGHT,
144:             Properties.COLOR,
145:             Properties.FONT_STYLE,
146:             Properties.FONT_DESIGN,
147:             Properties.UNDERLINE,
148:             Properties.STRIKETHROUGH,
149:         )
150: 
151:         private fun isSupported(attribute: TextAttribute): Boolean =
152:             attribute.property in SUPPORTED
153: 
154:         @JvmStatic fun plain(text: String) = AttributedString(text, emptyList(), emptyList())
155: 
156:         @JvmStatic
157:         fun of(text: String, runs: List<StyleRun>, links: List<LinkRun>) =
158:             AttributedString(text, runs, links)
159: 
160:         /** Start a range-tracking builder (inputs are Kotlin character indices). */
161:         @JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder = Builder()
162: 
163:         /** Decode a native markdown payload (UTF-8 byte offsets already). */
164:         @JvmStatic
165:         fun decode(payload: ByteArray): AttributedString {
166:             var p = 0
167:             fun need(n: Int) {
168:                 require(p + n <= payload.size) { "attributed text payload truncated" }
169:             }
170:             fun i32(): Int {
171:                 need(4)
172:                 val value = (payload[p].toInt() and 0xFF) or
173:                     ((payload[p + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
174:                     ((payload[p + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
175:                     ((payload[p + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
176:                 p += 4
177:                 return value
178:             }
179:             fun i16(): Int {
180:                 need(2)
181:                 val value = (payload[p].toInt() and 0xFF) or
182:                     ((payload[p + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8)
183:                 p += 2
184:                 return value
185:             }
186:             fun bytes(n: Int): ByteArray {
187:                 need(n)
188:                 val value = payload.copyOfRange(p, p + n)
189:                 p += n
190:                 return value
191:             }
192: 
193:             val textLen = i32()
194:             val text = String(bytes(textLen), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
195:             val runCount = i32()
196:             val runs = ArrayList<StyleRun>(runCount)
197:             repeat(runCount) {
198:                 val start = i32()
199:                 val end = i32()
200:                 val attrCount = i32()
201:                 val attributes = ArrayList<TextAttribute>(attrCount)
202:                 repeat(attrCount) {
203:                     val property = i16()
204:                     val valueType = payload[p++].toInt() and 0xFF
205:                     p++ // reserved
206:                     val value = i32()
207:                     val attribute = TextAttribute(property, valueType, value)
208:                     if (isSupported(attribute)) {
209:                         attributes.add(attribute)
210:                     }
211:                 }
212:                 runs.add(StyleRun(start, end, attributes))
213:             }
214:             val linkCount = i32()
215:             val links = ArrayList<LinkRun>(linkCount)
216:             repeat(linkCount) {
217:                 val start = i32()
218:                 val end = i32()
219:                 val urlLen = i32()
220:                 val url = String(bytes(urlLen), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
221:                 links.add(LinkRun(start, end, url))
222:             }
223:             return AttributedString(text, runs, links)
224:         }
225:     }
226: 
227:     /** Range-tracking builder: append text, then mark character ranges. */
228:     class Builder internal constructor() {
229:         private val text = StringBuilder()
230:         private val runs = ArrayList<StyleRun>()
231:         private val links = ArrayList<LinkRun>()
232: 
233:         fun append(value: String): Builder {
234:             text.append(value)
235:             return this
236:         }
237: 
238:         fun bold(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.fontWeight(700f))
239:         fun italic(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.italic())
240:         fun monospaced(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.fontDesign(3))
241:         fun underline(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.underline())
242:         fun strikethrough(start: Int, end: Int): Builder =
243:             style(start, end, TextAttribute.strikethrough())
244: 
245:         fun fontSize(start: Int, end: Int, points: Float): Builder =
246:             style(start, end, TextAttribute.fontSize(points))
247: 
248:         fun color(start: Int, end: Int, argb: Int): Builder =
249:             style(start, end, TextAttribute.color(argb))
250: 
251:         fun link(start: Int, end: Int, url: String): Builder {
252:             links.add(LinkRun(byteOffset(start), byteOffset(end), url))
253:             return this
254:         }
255: 
256:         private fun style(start: Int, end: Int, attribute: TextAttribute): Builder {
257:             runs.add(
258:                 StyleRun(byteOffset(start), byteOffset(end), listOf(attribute)),
259:             )
260:             return this
261:         }
262: 
263:         private fun byteOffset(charIndex: Int): Int {
264:             val value = text.toString()
265:             require(charIndex in 0..value.length) { "character index $charIndex is out of range" }
266:             return value.substring(0, charIndex).toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).size
267:         }
268: 
269:         fun build(): AttributedString =
270:             AttributedString(text.toString(), runs.toList(), links.toList())
271:     }
272: }

275:     write(value and 0xFF)
276:     write((value ushr 8) and 0xFF)
277:     write((value ushr 16) and 0xFF)
278:     write((value ushr 24) and 0xFF)
279: }

5: 
6: /**
7:  * A self-contained frame: 16-byte opcodes plus its own string section. STRING
8:  * payloads reference strings by a relative offset, so a frame decodes with no
9:  * prior state.
10:  */
11: data class ProtocolFrame(
12:     val opcodes: List<Opcode>,
13:     val strings: ByteArray,
14: ) {
15:     fun opcodes(): List<Opcode> = opcodes
16:     fun strings(): ByteArray = strings
17: 
18:     fun isEmpty(): Boolean = opcodes.isEmpty()
19: 
20:     /** Read a length-prefixed string at a relative offset in the string section. */
21:     fun stringAt(offset: Int): String {
22:         val len = readIntLE(strings, offset)
23:         return String(strings, offset + 4, len, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
24:     }
25: 
26:     companion object {
27:         @JvmField
28:         val EMPTY = ProtocolFrame(emptyList(), ByteArray(0))
29: 
30:         private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
31:             (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
32:                 ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
33:                 ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
34:                 ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
35:     }
36: }

1: package dev.pathland.view.core.transport
2: 
3: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Categories
4: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands
5: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Opcode
6: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.TokenPath
7: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.ValueEncoder
8: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.ValueTypes
9: import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
10: import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
11: 
12: /** An [OpcodeSink] that accumulates a self-contained [ProtocolFrame]. */
13: open class FrameOpcodeSink : OpcodeSink {
14:     private val opcodes = ArrayList<Opcode>()
15:     private val strings = ByteArrayOutputStream()
16:     private var frame: ProtocolFrame = ProtocolFrame.EMPTY
17:     private var framesProduced = 0
18: 
19:     fun frame(): ProtocolFrame = frame
20:     fun framesProduced(): Int = framesProduced
21:     fun hasChanges(): Boolean = opcodes.isNotEmpty()
22: 
23:     override fun beginFrame() {
24:         opcodes.clear()
25:         strings.reset()
26:     }
27: 
28:     override fun endFrame() {
29:         frame = ProtocolFrame(opcodes.toList(), strings.toByteArray())
30:         framesProduced++
31:     }
32: 
33:     override fun createNode(id: Int, component: Int) {
34:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0)
35:     }
36: 
37:     override fun deleteNode(id: Int) {
38:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0)
39:     }
40: 
41:     override fun insertChild(parent: Int, child: Int, index: Int) {
42:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index)
43:     }
44: 
45:     override fun removeChild(parent: Int, child: Int) {
46:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0)
47:     }
48: 
49:     override fun moveChild(parent: Int, child: Int, newIndex: Int) {
50:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex)
51:     }
52: 
53:     override fun setText(nodeId: Int, text: String) {
54:         val offset = strings.size()
55:         writeString(text)
56:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, offset, 0)
57:     }
58: 
59:     override fun setAttributedText(nodeId: Int, value: dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString) {
60:         val offset = strings.size()
61:         val payload = value.encode()
62:         writeIntLE(payload.size)
63:         strings.writeBytes(payload)
64:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT, 0, nodeId, offset, 0)
65:     }
66: 
67:     override fun setProperty(nodeId: Int, property: Int, valueType: Int, value: Any) {
68:         val b = (valueType shl 16) or (property and 0xFFFF)
69:         when (valueType) {
70:             ValueTypes.STRING -> {
71:                 val offset = strings.size()
72:                 writeString(value as String)
73:                 push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset)
74:             }
75:             ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN -> {
76:                 val offset = strings.size()
77:                 writeString((value as TokenPath).tokenPath() ?: "")
78:                 push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset)
79:             }
80:             ValueTypes.LIST -> {
81:                 val offset = strings.size()
82:                 val elements = value as FloatArray
83:                 writeIntLE(elements.size)
84:                 for (element in elements) {
85:                     val bits = element.toRawBits()
86:                     strings.write(bits and 0xFF)
87:                     strings.write((bits ushr 8) and 0xFF)
88:                     strings.write((bits ushr 16) and 0xFF)
89:                     strings.write((bits ushr 24) and 0xFF)
90:                 }
91:                 push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset)
92:             }
93:             else -> push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
94:                 ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value))
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:     override fun setDate(nodeId: Int, days: Int, millisOfDay: Int) {
99:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay)
100:     }
101: 
102:     override fun setDesignToken(path: String, valueType: Int, value: Any) {
103:         val pathOffset = strings.size()
104:         writeString(path)
105:         val c = if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
106:             val offset = strings.size()
107:             writeString(value as String)
108:             offset
109:         } else {
110:             ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value)
111:         }
112:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, 0, pathOffset, valueType, c)
113:     }
114: 
115:     fun writeString(text: String): Int {
116:         val offset = strings.size()
117:         val utf8 = text.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
118:         writeIntLE(utf8.size)
119:         strings.writeBytes(utf8)
120:         return offset
121:     }
122: 
123:     private fun push(category: Int, command: Int, flags: Int, a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) {
124:         opcodes.add(Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c))
125:     }
126: 
127:     private fun writeIntLE(value: Int) {
128:         strings.write(value and 0xFF)
129:         strings.write((value ushr 8) and 0xFF)
130:         strings.write((value ushr 16) and 0xFF)
131:         strings.write((value ushr 24) and 0xFF)
132:     }
133: 
134:     override fun resetTheme() {
135:         push(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.RESET_THEME, 0, 0, 0, 0)
136:     }
137: 
138:     override fun setColorScheme(mode: Int) {
139:         push(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.SET_COLOR_SCHEME, 0, mode, 0, 0)
140:     }
141: 
142:     override fun setWindowMetadata(field: Int, value: String) {
143:         val offset = strings.size()
144:         writeString(value)
145:         push(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.SET_WINDOW_METADATA, 0, field, offset, 0)
146:     }
147: }

1: package dev.pathland.view.core.transport
2: 
3: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Categories
4: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands
5: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Opcode
6: import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
7: import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
8: 
9: /** The network batch codec — mirrors `pathland_core_transport`. */
10: object FrameCodec {
11:     const val MAGIC = 0x504C_504C
12:     const val VERSION = 1
13:     const val GUEST_TO_HOST = 0x0000
14:     const val HOST_TO_GUEST = 0x0001
15:     const val HEADER = 16
16: 
17:     /** Encode a self-contained frame as a network batch (sequence 0). */
18:     @JvmStatic
19:     fun encodeFrame(frame: ProtocolFrame): ByteArray = encodeFrame(frame, 0)
20: 
21:     /** Encode a self-contained frame as a guest → host batch with [sequence]. */
22:     @JvmStatic
23:     fun encodeFrame(frame: ProtocolFrame, sequence: Int): ByteArray {
24:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
25:         writeHeader(out, GUEST_TO_HOST, sequence, frame.opcodes.size)
26:         for (op in frame.opcodes) {
27:             writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())
28:         }
29:         writeIntLE(out, frame.strings.size)
30:         writeBytes(out, frame.strings)
31:         return out.toByteArray()
32:     }
33: 
34:     /** Decode a self-contained frame batch into opcodes + string section. */
35:     @JvmStatic
36:     fun decodeFrame(bytes: ByteArray): ProtocolFrame {
37:         val parsed = parse(bytes)
38:         return ProtocolFrame(parsed.opcodes, parsed.strings)
39:     }
40: 
41:     /** The per-stream message sequence encoded in a batch header (offset 8). */
42:     @JvmStatic
43:     fun sequence(bytes: ByteArray): Int {
44:         if (bytes.size < HEADER) throw IllegalArgumentException("batch truncated")
45:         return readIntLE(bytes, 8)
46:     }
47: 
48:     /** Encode a `META::RESYNC` request batch (host → guest). */
49:     @JvmStatic
50:     fun encodeResync(): ByteArray = singleMeta(Commands.Meta.RESYNC)
51: 
52:     /** Encode a `META::PONG` reply batch (host → guest). */
53:     @JvmStatic
54:     fun encodePong(): ByteArray = singleMeta(Commands.Meta.PONG)
55: 
56:     /** Encode a `META::PING` heartbeat probe batch (guest → host). */
57:     @JvmStatic
58:     fun encodePing(): ByteArray {
59:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
60:         writeHeader(out, GUEST_TO_HOST, 0, 1)
61:         writeBytes(out, Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.PING, 0, 0, 0, 0).toBytes())
62:         writeIntLE(out, 0)
63:         return out.toByteArray()
64:     }
65: 
66:     private fun singleMeta(command: Int): ByteArray {
67:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
68:         writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, 1)
69:         writeBytes(out, Opcode(Categories.META, command, 0, 0, 0, 0).toBytes())
70:         writeIntLE(out, 0)
71:         return out.toByteArray()
72:     }
73: 
74:     /** Encode a `META::ENVIRONMENT` field batch (viewport + route). */
75:     @JvmStatic
76:     fun encodeEnvironment(env: EnvironmentData): ByteArray {
77:         val route = env.route.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
78:         val ops = ArrayList<Opcode>(3)
79:         if (env.viewportWidth > 0) {
80:             ops.add(Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT, 0,
81:                 Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_WIDTH, env.viewportWidth.toRawBits(), 0))
82:         }
83:         if (env.viewportHeight > 0) {
84:             ops.add(Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT, 0,
85:                 Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_HEIGHT, env.viewportHeight.toRawBits(), 0))
86:         }
87:         ops.add(Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT, 0,
88:             Commands.Environment.ROUTE, 0, 0))
89:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
90:         writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, ops.size)
91:         for (op in ops) {
92:             writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())
93:         }
94:         writeIntLE(out, 4 + route.size)
95:         writeIntLE(out, route.size)
96:         out.writeBytes(route)
97:         return out.toByteArray()
98:     }
99: 
100:     /** True when the batch is a `META::RESYNC` request. */
101:     @JvmStatic
102:     fun isResync(bytes: ByteArray): Boolean =
103:         parse(bytes).opcodes.any { it.category == Categories.META && it.command == Commands.Meta.RESYNC }
104: 
105:     /** True when the batch carries a `META::PING` heartbeat probe. */
106:     @JvmStatic
107:     fun isPing(bytes: ByteArray): Boolean =
108:         parse(bytes).opcodes.any { it.category == Categories.META && it.command == Commands.Meta.PING }
109: 
110:     /** True when the batch carries `META::ENVIRONMENT` fields. */

9: /** A declarative path → destination table with params and guards. */
10: class RouteTable private constructor(
11:     private val entries: List<Entry>,
12:     private val fallback: RouteHandler?,
13: ) {
14:     /** Match an absolute path, returning the first match or the fallback. */
15:     fun match(path: String): Optional<RouteMatch> {
16:         val pathOnly = Route.of(path).pathOnly()
17:         for (entry in entries) {
18:             val params = entry.match(pathOnly)
19:             if (!params.isPresent) continue
20:             val captured = params.get()
21:             if (entry.guard != null && !entry.guard.test(captured)) {
22:                 return Optional.of(RouteMatch.redirect(entry.redirect))
23:             }
24:             return Optional.of(RouteMatch(pathOnly, captured, entry.handler, null))
25:         }
26:         return if (fallback != null) {
27:             Optional.of(RouteMatch(pathOnly, Params.none(), fallback, null))
28:         } else {
29:             Optional.empty()
30:         }
31:     }
32: 
33:     /** A match: either a destination (handler + params) or a guard redirect. */
34:     data class RouteMatch(
35:         val path: String?,
36:         val params: Params,
37:         val handler: RouteHandler?,
38:         val redirect: String?,
39:     ) {
40:         fun path(): String? = path
41:         fun params(): Params = params
42:         fun handler(): RouteHandler? = handler
43:         fun redirect(): String? = redirect
44: 
45:         /** True when a guard redirected this match (replace, not mount). */
46:         fun isRedirect(): Boolean = redirect != null
47: 
48:         companion object {
49:             internal fun redirect(target: String?): RouteMatch =
50:                 RouteMatch(null, Params.none(), null, target)
51:         }
52:     }
53: 
54:     /** Builds a RouteTable. */
55:     class Builder {
56:         private val entries = ArrayList<Entry>()
57:         private var fallback: RouteHandler? = null
58: 
59:         fun route(pattern: String, view: View): Builder {
60:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, RouteHandler { view }, null, null))
61:             return this
62:         }
63: 
64:         fun route(pattern: String, handler: RouteHandler): Builder {
65:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, handler, null, null))
66:             return this
67:         }
68: 
69:         fun route(pattern: String, guard: Predicate<Params>, redirect: String?, view: View): Builder {
70:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, RouteHandler { view }, Objects.requireNonNull(guard, "guard"), redirect))
71:             return this
72:         }
73: 
74:         fun route(pattern: String, guard: Predicate<Params>, redirect: String?, handler: RouteHandler): Builder {
75:             entries.add(Entry(pattern, handler, Objects.requireNonNull(guard, "guard"), redirect))
76:             return this
77:         }
78: 
79:         fun fallback(view: View): Builder = fallback(RouteHandler { view })
80: 
81:         fun fallback(handler: RouteHandler): Builder {
82:             this.fallback = Objects.requireNonNull(handler, "fallback")
83:             return this
84:         }
85: 
86:         fun build(): RouteTable = RouteTable(entries.toList(), fallback)
87:     }
88: 
89:     private class Entry(
90:         pattern: String,
91:         val handler: RouteHandler,
92:         val guard: Predicate<Params>?,
93:         val redirect: String?,
94:     ) {
95:         private val segments = parse(pattern)
96: 
97:         fun match(path: String): Optional<Params> {
98:             val given = split(path)
99:             if (given.size != segments.size) return Optional.empty()
100:             val params = LinkedHashMap<String, String>()
101:             for (i in segments.indices) {
102:                 if (!segments[i].matches(given[i], params)) return Optional.empty()
103:             }
104:             return Optional.of(Params.of(params, path))
105:         }
106: 
107:         companion object {
108:             private fun parse(pattern: String): List<Segment> =
109:                 split(pattern).map { part ->
110:                     if (part.startsWith(":")) Segment.Param(part.substring(1))
111:                     else Segment.Literal(part)
112:                 }
113: 
114:             private fun split(path: String): Array<String> {
115:                 val trimmed = if (path.startsWith("/")) path.substring(1) else path
116:                 return if (trimmed.isEmpty()) emptyArray() else trimmed.split("/").toTypedArray()
117:             }
118:         }
119:     }
120: 
121:     private sealed interface Segment {
122:         fun matches(part: String, params: MutableMap<String, String>): Boolean
123: 
124:         class Literal(private val value: String) : Segment {
125:             override fun matches(part: String, params: MutableMap<String, String>): Boolean = value == part
126:         }
127: 
128:         class Param(private val name: String) : Segment {
129:             override fun matches(part: String, params: MutableMap<String, String>): Boolean {
130:                 params[name] = part
131:                 return true
132:             }
133:         }
134:     }
135: 
136:     companion object {
137:         /** Start building a route table. */
138:         fun builder(): Builder = Builder()
139:     }
140: }

22:     /** Dispatch every event in a decoded batch. */
23:     fun dispatch(events: Iterable<Event>) {
24:         for (event in events) dispatch(event)
25:     }

27:     /** Route a single raw input event into the app's bindings. */
28:     fun dispatch(event: Event) {
29:         when {
30:             event.isPointerUp -> {
31:                 val nav = navigateActions[event.target()]
32:                 if (nav != null) nav.run()

4: import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.WireValue
5: import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal
6: import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
7: 
8: /** Converts a reactive signal's value into the typed property value stored on a node. */
9: object ReactiveValues {
10:     /** Read the signal for an initial render value without subscribing the component. */
11:     fun initial(property: Int, signal: Signal<*>): Any? =
12:         Signals.untracked { from(property, signal) }
13: 
14:     /** Read the signal and normalize its value for storage as a node property. */
15:     fun from(property: Int, signal: Signal<*>): Any? {
16:         var value: Any? = signal.get()
17:         if (value is Boolean) {
18:             value = if (value) 1 else 0
19:         } else if (value is WireValue) {
20:             value = value.wire()
21:         }
22:         return coerce(property, value)
23:     }
24: 
25:     private fun coerce(property: Int, value: Any?): Any? =
26:         when (ValueTypes.forProperty(property)) {
27:             ValueTypes.F32 -> toFloat(property, value)
28:             ValueTypes.U8, ValueTypes.U32, ValueTypes.I32, ValueTypes.ENUM -> toInt(property, value)
29:             ValueTypes.COLOR, ValueTypes.STRING, ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN -> value
30:             else -> value
31:         }
32: 
33:     private fun toFloat(property: Int, value: Any?): Float = when (value) {
34:         is Float -> value
35:         is Int -> value.toFloat()
36:         is Double -> value.toFloat()
37:         else -> throw unsupported(property, value)
38:     }
39: 
40:     private fun toInt(property: Int, value: Any?): Int = when (value) {
41:         is Int -> value
42:         is Float -> value.toInt()
43:         else -> throw unsupported(property, value)
44:     }
45: 
46:     private fun unsupported(property: Int, value: Any?): IllegalArgumentException =
47:         IllegalArgumentException(
48:             "Unsupported reactive property value $value for property 0x${Integer.toHexString(property)}",
49:         )
50: }

# The demo modules live in the default-active `demos` profile. Activating
      # `release` deactivates it, so the reactor contains only publishable modules
      # (central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles every reactor module).
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: mvn -B -P release deploy

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
          ls -la dist/jars

      - name: Upload the main jars
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: jars
          path: dist/jars/*.jar

## Local pre-flight

Rust — `cargo publish --dry-run -p pathland-core` validates the leaf crate (the
dependent crates can only be dry-run once their dependencies are on crates.io,
so the ordered CI publish validates them).

Java — `mvn -P release verify` builds and signs the sources/javadoc jars without
uploading. It needs GPG installed and a `central` server in `~/.m2/settings.xml`.
The `pathland-view-core` javadoc jar is generated with **Dokka** (the module is
Kotlin-first and JDK javadoc cannot resolve Kotlin declarations); the pure-Java
modules use `maven-javadoc-plugin`. Both run only under the `release` profile:

```xml
<server>
  <id>central</id>
  <username>TOKEN_USERNAME</username>
  <password>TOKEN_PASSWORD</password>
</server>
```

## Publishable crates (dependency order)

```
pathland-core → pathland-markdown → pathland-engine → pathland-view → pathland-render-core → pathland-core-transport → pathland-render-html
```

(`pathland-view-native`, `pathland-core-capi`, `pathland-markdown-capi`,
`pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-qt`, `pathland-render-gtk-demo`,
`pathland-engine-golden`, `pathland-html-golden`, `pathland-protocol-manifest`,
`pathland-ts-codegen` are **not** published — C-ABI cdylibs, native renderers,
and dev tools.) `pathland-render-core` **is** published because
`pathland-core-transport` has it as a dev-dependency, and Cargo requires every
dev-dependency to resolve from the registry at publish time.

`scripts/check-release-crates.sh` verifies this list against `cargo metadata`
(no unpublished path dependency, correct order). It runs in CI.

## Published Java modules

`pathland-view-core` (Kotlin JVM engine/SPI + the sole authoring DSL),
`pathland-render-html`, `pathland-server-core` (runtime, telemetry adapters,
Redis state store, and the shared WS test harness), `pathland-spring-boot-starter`,
`pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-quarkus-deployment` (plus the `pathland-parent`
POM). The demo modules (`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`, `pathland-desktop-demo`,
`pathland-quarkus-demo`, `pathland-spring-boot-demo`) set `maven.deploy.skip`.

## Project map

- `lib/rust/` — the Rust workspace: `pathland-core` (protocol), `pathland-markdown`
  (shared inline Markdown), `pathland-markdown-capi` (C ABI), `pathland-engine`
  (emitter/signals), `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-core-capi` (C ABI),
  `pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-view-native`,
  `pathland-render-gtk-demo`.
- `lib/java/` — the Maven reactor: `pathland-view-core`
  (Kotlin `dev.pathland.view.core*`, `dev.pathland.view.engine`, and the sole
  JVM authoring DSL `dev.pathland.view.dsl`), `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` (the
  Kotlin music player, ad app, shared theme and assets), `pathland-render-html`,
  `pathland-server-core` (runtime + telemetry + Redis + shared WS test harness),
  the `pathland-quarkus` extension, the desktop (GTK/Qt) and Quarkus/Spring
  demos, and the TypeScript DOM renderer (`lib/typescript`).
- `spec/` — the protocol contract: `OPCODE.md` (primary), `PRIMITIVES.md`,
  `MODIFIERS.md`, `EVENTS.md`, `CONFORMANCE.md` (golden vectors), `ENGINE.md`
  (retained-tree behavior), `DSL.md` (authoring surface), `protocol.tsv` (the
  target-neutral ID manifest), and `engine-traces/` (shared frame fixtures).

Implementation status per project lives in each crate/module's `status.md`.

## Prerequisites

- **Rust**: stable toolchain (`rustup`); `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target for the
  `no_std` direction guard.

**Premise correction:** the protocol engine is *already* Kotlin on the JVM. `pathland-view-core` implements opcodes, the diff emitter, signals, the `PLPL` codec, and is byte-checked against Rust by `ProtocolManifestTest` + `EngineTraceTest`. The JVM server path only pulls in **two** Rust dylibs through JNA:

- `libpathland_render_html` (`pathland-render-html`, ~5.9k LOC) — the real question
- `libpathland_markdown` (`pathland-markdown`, ~520 LOC)

So this is not "Rust protocol vs Kotlin protocol"; it's "keep the SSR HTML renderer in Rust, or reimplement it in Kotlin." The renderer is a pure function of the frame and depends only on `pathland-core`/`pathland-core-transport`, so a port is mechanically feasible.

## Does GraalVM care? Yes — mainly packaging, not speed

Today nothing targets native-image: CI is JVM-only and the Quarkus `Dockerfile` ships a JRE + jars. If you add Quarkus/Spring native later:

- **JNA itself works** under `native-image` (JNA 5.14 ships metadata), but it is not zero-config: reachability/reflection for the `Library` interface plus resource registration for the embedded dylib.
- The jar-extraction path (`getResourceAsStream("/META-INF/native/...")` → temp dir) needs `quarkus.native.resources.includes=META-INF/native/**`, and breaks in hardened containers with read-only/noexec `/tmp`.
- Avoiding extraction means shipping the `.so`/`.dylib` beside the executable and setting `-Dpathland.render.html.lib=...` — which forfeits the "single binary" benefit native images are for.
- A **pure Kotlin renderer** AOT-compiles in: no JNA, no dlopen, no resource extraction, no sidecar lib, one executable. That is a genuine operational difference.
- Runtime performance is a wash (the Rust code is already native); only minor JNA startup/init differs.

## Tradeoffs of porting

- Output must stay **byte-identical**: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-html-golden` treats Rust SSR as canonical and the TS DOM client asserts the same fixtures. A Kotlin port needs a golden test against those fixtures before it can be trusted.
- It creates a second SSR implementation. The repo deliberately removed the Java renderer (`e9aade28`) for a "single renderer, every language" story. The Rust crate is still the cross-language/C-ABI projection target for non-JVM hosts.
- Feature velocity: every new component/property must land in both renderers (mitigated by the golden harness — the TS client already proves cross-renderer drift is testable).

## Recommendation

- **If GraalVM native is on the roadmap now:** port `pathland-render-html` to Kotlin in the JVM module, keep the Rust crate for non-JVM hosts, and wire `pathland-html-golden` into both (port `pathland-markdown` too — it's tiny). This gives you true single-binary native images.
- **If native is speculative:** don't port. Keep the one Rust renderer and add native-image config only when needed (resource include + `pathland.render.html.lib` sidecar). Porting now is a large change for no current deployment gain.
- The protocol should stay where it is (Kotlin on the JVM, Rust canonical for non-JVM); there is no benefit to moving that.

## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
  `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
  `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
  `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
- **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
  `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
  modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
  router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
  nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
  error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
  stack still drives auto-registration.
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,

- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,

@ Target ( allowedTargets = [ AnnotationTarget.ANNOTATION_CLASS ] )
annotation class DslMarker ( source )
When applied to annotation class X specifies that X defines a DSL language
The general rule:
* an implicit receiver may belong to a DSL @X if marked with a corresponding DSL marker annotation
* two implicit receivers of the same DSL are not accessible in the same scope
* the closest one wins
* other available receivers are resolved as usual, but if the resulting resolved call binds to such a receiver, it's a compilation error
Marking rules: an implicit receiver is considered marked with @Ann if
* its type is marked, or
* its type's classifier is marked
* or any of its superclasses/superinterfaces

DslMarker

kotlin-stdlib / kotlin / DslMarker
Platform and version requirements: JVM (1.1), JS (1.1), Native (1.1)
@Target([AnnotationTarget.ANNOTATION_CLASS]) annotation class DslMarker
When applied to annotation class X specifies that X defines a DSL language
The general rule:
* an implicit receiver may belong to a DSL @X if marked with a corresponding DSL marker annotation
* two implicit receivers of the same DSL are not accessible in the same scope
* the closest one wins
* other available receivers are resolved as usual, but if the resulting resolved call binds to such a receiver, it's a compilation error
Marking rules: an implicit receiver is considered marked with @Ann if
* its type is marked, or
* its type's classifier is marked
* or any of its superclasses/superinterfaces

# Plan: split `pathland-view-core` into a pure-Java `pathland-core` + Kotlin DSL `pathland-view-core`

## Target architecture

```
lib/java/
  pathland-core/                    # NEW — pure Java 17, no Kotlin source
    dev.pathland.core.*             # protocol, transport, signal, state, subscription,
                                    # router, SPI/value types (View/Environment/Color/…)
    dev.pathland.core.engine.*      # Emitter, PathlandNode, ViewSlot, RenderResult, …
    dev.pathland.core.markdown.*    # pure-Java Markdown parser
  pathland-view-core/               # KEPT — Kotlin DSL only
    dev.pathland.view.dsl.*         # builders, modifiers, Component, Scope, Styles
```

`pathland-view-core` depends on `pathland-core`; downstream modules depend on whichever they actually use. No protocol/spec semantics change — this is a package/module/language refactor only.

## Package mapping

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `dev.pathland.view.core` | `dev.pathland.core` |
| `dev.pathland.view.core.protocol` | `dev.pathland.core.protocol` |
| `dev.pathland.view.core.transport` | `dev.pathland.core.transport` |
| `dev.pathland.view.core.signal` | `dev.pathland.core.signal` |
| `dev.pathland.view.core.state` | `dev.pathland.core.state` |
| `dev.pathland.view.core.subscription` | `dev.pathland.core.subscription` |
| `dev.pathland.view.core.router` | `dev.pathland.core.router` |
| `dev.pathland.view.engine` | `dev.pathland.core.engine` |
| `dev.pathland.markdown` | `dev.pathland.core.markdown` |
| `dev.pathland.view.dsl` | unchanged |

## Files to move/port (all Kotlin → Java unless noted)

- **protocol (9):** Categories, Commands (+ nested groups), Components, Opcode, Properties, TokenPath, ValueEncoder, ValueTypes, WireValue
- **signal (14):** Signal, WritableSignal, WritableSignalImpl, ConstantSignal, ReactiveNode, ReactiveContext, ComputedSignal, Effect, EffectRef, EffectException, EffectOptions, Scheduler, Signals, Tracked
- **state (4):** StateStore, InMemoryStateStore, StateStoreProvider, PersistentState
- **subscription (3):** Topic, SessionContext, GlobalSubject
- **transport (6):** OpcodeSink, ProtocolFrame, Event, EnvironmentData, FrameOpcodeSink, FrameCodec
- **router (11):** Chrome, Navigation, NavigationContainer, NavigationIntent, NavigationIntentView, NavOp, Params, Route, RouteHandler, Router, RouteTable
- **core SPI/value types (~54):** View, ViewModifier, Configurable, ChildrenView, Modified, ViewBuilder, EmptyContent, ReactiveSlotView, Environment*, Theme*/AdaptiveTheme, MediaController, WindowMetadata, ProxyConfig, Color, Length, Platform, PathlandDsl, Style, Roles, all enums (`Alignment`, `FontWeight`, `Truncation`, …), `AttributedString`/`TextAttribute`/`StyleRun`/`LinkRun`, `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`VideoStyle`, `TapGesture*`, `PointerEvents*`, `PathChange*`, `FontFamily`/`FontWidth`
- **engine (8):** Emitter, PathlandNode, ViewSlot, RenderResult, InputDispatcher, ReactiveValues, DateInput, MediaInput
- **markdown (1, already Java):** `Markdown.java` (`git mv`)

Tests:
- **Move to `pathland-core/src/test/java`:** `MarkdownTest`, `ProtocolManifestTest`, `SignalsTest`, `PersistentStateTest`, `FrameCodecTest`; port `SignalsStateTest.kt` to Java.
- **Keep in `pathland-view-core`:** `DslTest.kt`, `EngineTraceTest.kt`, `MediaProjectionTest.kt` (imports updated).

## Java porting / interop rules (critical — Kotlin DSL calls into Java)

1. **Preserve Kotlin property access.** Every former Kotlin `val/var` gets a conventional Java getter/setter (`getText()`, `isPlain()`, `setText()`), *in addition to* existing explicit accessors (`text()`, `argb()`, `wire()`). This keeps both Kotlin DSL (`node.text`, `value.isPlain`) and Java hosts (`event.target()`) compiling.
2. **Keep `@JvmField`-style public fields** on `PathlandNode` (DSL reads/writes `node.text`, `node.properties`, `node.children`, but engine also uses them directly).
3. **Data classes** (`Opcode`, `Event`, `Route`, `Color`, `Length`, `EffectOptions`, `TextAttribute`, `StyleRun`, `LinkRun`, `ProxyConfig`, `RenderResult`, `RouteMatch`, …) implement `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`; tests and `IdentityHashMap`/`Set` behavior depend on `Opcode` equality especially.
4. **Functional interfaces** (`Signal`, `ViewModifier`, `RouteHandler`, `DateInput`) become Java `@FunctionalInterface`s so Kotlin SAM lambdas (`Signal { … }`, `Signals.effect { … }`) keep working.
5. **`GlobalSubject`** (Kotlin `object` used as a value) → Java singleton with `public static final GlobalSubject INSTANCE` + `NAME`; update Kotlin call sites (`Signals.kt`, `dsl/Signals.kt`, server tests) to `GlobalSubject.INSTANCE`. Java already uses `.INSTANCE`.
6. **`Params`** loses `operator get`; no external `params["x"]` usages exist, so this is safe.
7. **`GlobalTopic` typealias** is unused → drop it.
8. **`@PathlandDsl`** → Java annotation `@interface` meta-annotated with `@kotlin.DslMarker` (Spring Integration does exactly this). Add `kotlin-stdlib` as `provided` to `pathland-core` for that one annotation; keep `@Target({TYPE, TYPE_USE})`, `RetentionPolicy.CLASS`.
9. **`internal` visibility:** same-package members become package-private; cross-package members used by the engine (`Environment.setWindowMetadata`-style) become public with an “internal API” doc note.
10. **Kotlin-only conveniences** (`copy()`, destructuring, receiver lambdas, typealiases) must be re-expressed; the DSL does not use `copy()`/destructuring on core types (confirmed), so this is limited.

## Module / POM changes

1. **New `pathland-core/pom.xml`:** parent `pathland-parent`, artifactId `pathland-core`, `maven.compiler.release=17`, JUnit test dep, `kotlin-stdlib` `provided` (only for `@DslMarker`), **no Kotlin plugin, no Dokka**. JDK javadoc via parent.
2. **Parent `lib/java/pom.xml`:** add `<module>pathland-core</module>` before `pathland-view-core`; update the reactor description.
3. **`pathland-view-core/pom.xml`:** add compile dependency on `pathland-core`; remove `src/main/java` from Kotlin source dirs (only Markdown lived there); keep Kotlin plugin + Dokka release profile (DSL is still Kotlin); update name/description.
4. **Downstream POMs:** `pathland-native-core` and `pathland-state-redis` switch to `pathland-core` only; `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-server-core`, starters, Quarkus use `pathland-core` compile + `pathland-view-core` (compile if main DSL, test scope if DSL only in tests); demos keep `pathland-view-core`.
5. **Release/CI:** add `pathland-core` to `.github/workflows/release.yml` jar collection; update `RELEASING.md` published-module list; keep Dokka for view-core, JDK javadoc for core.

## Downstream source updates

- Rewrite every import in `pathland-native-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter`, `pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`, `pathland-desktop-demo`, and both demos.
- `ProtocolManifestTest` hard-codes `"dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands$"` → `"dev.pathland.core.protocol.Commands$"`.
- Update DSL-internal fully-qualified references (`dev.pathland.view.core.Color.argb(…)` in `Views.kt`, etc.).

## Docs

- Add `lib/java/pathland-core/status.md`; rewrite `lib/java/pathland-view-core/status.md` for the DSL-only module (remove the “one module / package boundary” note).
- Update `AGENTS.md` (architecture tree, module list, “engine/protocol live in pathland-core”, status).
- Update `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `lib/rust/README.md`, `spec/ENGINE.md`, `spec/DSL.md`, `spec/engine-traces/README.md`, `docs/HARDENING.md`, `docs/router-plan.md`, `SECURITY.md`, and Rust `status.md` references.
- No `spec/protocol.tsv`, `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, or engine-trace fixtures change.

## Execution sequence (each checkpoint keeps the build green)

1. **Scaffold** `pathland-core` + parent module entry; empty module builds.
2. **Port protocol + transport** (with `ProtocolManifestTest`, `FrameCodecTest`).
3. **Port signal + state + subscription** (with `SignalsTest`, `PersistentStateTest`, ported `SignalsStateTest`).
4. **Port core SPI/value types + router + AttributedString**.
5. **Port engine**; run `EngineTraceTest` from `pathland-view-core` against the new core.
6. **Move Markdown** (`dev.pathland.core.markdown`) + `MarkdownTest`.
7. **Switch** `dev.pathland.view.dsl` imports to `dev.pathland.core.*` / `.engine.*`; delete old `core`/`engine` Kotlin sources; update `view-core` tests.
8. **Update downstream modules** (imports + POM dependencies).
9. **Docs/CI/release** updates.
10. **Full verification.**

## Verification

```bash
cd lib/java
mvn -q -pl pathland-core -am test
mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core -am test
mvn -q -P jvm-only test          # libraries + starters, no demos
mvn -q test                      # full reactor incl. demos (build-time)
mvn -q -P release -Dgpg.skip=true -DskipTests package   # javadoc/dokka + reactor
```

Also confirm:
- `EngineTraceTest` is byte-for-byte green (proves the Java engine matches the Rust golden frames).
- `ProtocolManifestTest` is green after the package-string update.
- No `dev.pathland.view.core` / `dev.pathland.view.engine` / `dev.pathland.markdown` references remain (`grep -r`), except historical docs.
- `lib/rust` `cargo test` is untouched (no Rust changes).

## Risks & mitigations

- **Kotlin↔Java interop regressions** (property vs method names): enforce the getter+accessor rule; compile all modules at every checkpoint.
- **`@DslMarker` on a Java annotation**: Spring Integration proves it works; add a tiny compile check (`@PathlandDsl` on a DSL scope still rejects outer-receiver capture).
- **Engine behavior parity**: port mechanically; the golden traces are the safety net.
- **`GlobalSubject` / `Params` source incompatibilities**: update the handful of Kotlin call sites.
- **Dokka/javadoc**: core uses JDK javadoc; view-core keeps Dokka.
- **No native/JNA impact**: JNA remains isolated in `pathland-native-core`; core stays pure JVM.

## Assumptions (flag if wrong)

- Markdown moves into `pathland-core` as `dev.pathland.core.markdown` (engine needs it, and engine is in core).
- `dev.pathland.view.dsl` remains the only thing in `pathland-view-core`.
- Downstream modules change package imports (no compatibility shim / bridge classes are kept).

Would you like me to proceed with this sequence, or adjust the Markdown package / any of the porting conventions first?
Will ths have any downside to building views in kotlin?
